segments.speaker: You
segments.text: Morning everyone. First item is the search latency regression. Priya, what did you find?

segments.speaker: Person 3 (Priya Natarajan)
segments.text: The p95 went from about three hundred milliseconds to nine hundred after the index migration. The new index writes one document at a time, so every update pays a full round trip and the queue backs up during peak hours.

segments.speaker: Person 3 (Priya Natarajan)
segments.text: My proposal is batching the writes. We collect updates for fifty milliseconds and send them together. In staging that brought p95 back to two hundred eighty.

segments.speaker: Person 2 (Dana Reyes)
segments.text: That sounds right. Are there risks with ordering? Some customers depend on updates landing in sequence.

segments.speaker: Person 3 (Priya Natarajan)
segments.text: Ordering is preserved inside a batch and batches are sequential, so no change there.

segments.speaker: You
segments.text: Good. Decision then: we ship the batching fix on September 22. Priya owns it, Dana reviews.

segments.speaker: Person 4 (Lee Chen)
segments.text: On my side, the Acme Freight webhook retries keep failing. Their endpoint times out after five seconds and we retry immediately, which makes it worse. I'll add exponential backoff this week.

segments.speaker: Person 2 (Dana Reyes)
segments.text: One more thing from accounts. Bluegill Bank wants single sign-on before they roll out to their branches, ideally by Q4. Sam is tracking the request.

segments.speaker: You
segments.text: Let's scope SSO next week then. Lee, take the webhook backoff. Thanks all.
